title: Tamarind Kani Mustard Sauce
author: Pierre Thiam (via the Shepherd Song Farm site)
desc: Onion, garlic, plum tomatoes, a Scotch bonnet and a bay leaf simmered about 15 minutes, then tamarind paste, sugar and fish sauce stirred in and the sauce pureed smooth — the condiment for slow-roasted dibi lamb.
longDesc: Thiam’s tamarind kani sauce accompanies his dibi-style leg of lamb. A tablespoon of peanut oil cooks a coarsely chopped onion and a clove of garlic over medium-low heat, stirring often, until soft and fragrant; six plum tomatoes, a chopped Scotch bonnet and a dried bay leaf are added and simmered about 15 minutes, with a little water if needed. Tamarind paste, sugar and fish sauce go in; the sauce is seasoned, the bay leaf removed, and everything pureed until smooth. It makes about 1 cup and keeps up to 3 weeks airtight in the refrigerator. The title says ‘mustard sauce’ but the ingredient list contains no mustard (the lamb recipe, not this sauce, uses Dijon); this is flagged and not corrected.
ingredients: Salt and pepper, to taste — quantities not printed
steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Cook the onion and garlic, stirring often, until soft and fragrant. The page prints no time for this step.
Add the tomatoes, Scotch bonnet and bay leaf. Simmer about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally and adding a little water if needed, until thick like a chutney.
Stir in the tamarind paste, sugar and fish sauce. Season with salt and pepper. Remove the bay leaf and puree until smooth.
Store airtight in the refrigerator for up to 3 weeks.
chefTips: Three printed cues: ‘soft and fragrant’, ‘thick like a chutney’, ‘until smooth’.
Take out the bay leaf before blending.
Scotch bonnet heat varies; add it gradually.
commonMistakes: Looking for mustard in the sauce — the printed list has none.
Skipping the water top-up so the tomatoes catch.
Leaving the bay leaf in the blender.
healthBenefits: Tomatoes and tamarind add acidity; fish sauce adds salt.
culturalNote: ‘Kani’ is the Senegalese hot-pepper sauce family (compare sosu kaani, SEN090, and Mendy’s kanni, SEN093). This version is Thiam’s: tamarind and fish sauce give a sweet-sour savoury depth that the other two lack.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Tamarind Kani Mustard Sauce’ (with the lamb page titled ‘Slow Roasted Dibi Lamb Recipe’). Byline as printed: ‘Shepherd’ — a site persona, not a personal name; the page says the recipes are ‘Used with permission from Chef Pierre Thiam’, whose book ‘Senegal: Modern Senegalese Recipes from the Source to the Bowl’ is named. Published 25 August 2018; page metadata last modified 3 March 2025. Makes about 1 cup. SINGLE-PASS.
FLAG: the title says ‘Mustard Sauce’ but the printed ingredient list contains no mustard. Reported, not fixed.

Times: the onion step has NO printed time (cue only: ‘soft and fragrant’); the simmer is ‘about 15 minutes’. The 20-minute cook figure above is the 15 minutes plus a scheduling estimate of 5 minutes for the onion step, and the prep of 10 minutes is a scheduling estimate; neither is source data.
